title: Best Flooring for a Basement Remodel or ADU in Snohomish: Carpet, Vinyl or Both?
meta: Best flooring for a Snohomish basement or ADU is usually both: vinyl plank where water can reach, carpet where people sleep. Wills Flooring explains how to zone it.
keywords: best flooring for basement remodel Snohomish, ADU flooring carpet or vinyl, carpet in a basement below grade, vinyl plank vs carpet basement, DADU flooring Snohomish WA, basement bedroom carpet

blocks.lead: For most Snohomish basements and ADUs the right answer is both: vinyl plank in the kitchenette, bath, entry and laundry, and carpet in the bedrooms and the TV room.
blocks.detail: Concrete below grade in Snohomish County is rarely bone dry, and a rental ADU takes harder use than your own upstairs. Zone the floor by how wet and how busy each room will be, then pick the carpet spec and the plank spec that survive there.

blocks.html: The question usually arrives like this: "We're finishing the daylight basement on Fobes Hill for my mother-in-law" or "We're turning the shop on our Clearview acreage into a rental ADU. Carpet or vinyl?" Both are good floors. The mistake is treating the whole space as one decision. A basement in Snohomish has a concrete slab that breathes moisture, an exterior door that lets in mud and dog paws, and at least one room where somebody wants to walk barefoot. Those are three different floors.

blocks.text: Start with the slab, not the sample board

items.title: Moisture test the concrete
items.text: A calcium chloride or in-slab relative humidity test tells you how much vapor is coming up through the floor. Older Snohomish slabs often have no vapor barrier under them. A high reading does not rule out carpet or plank, but it decides the pad, the barrier and sometimes the glue.

items.title: Look for past water
items.text: Efflorescence (white powder), a tide line on the bottom of drywall, rust on the furnace feet or a musty smell near the sump all mean water has visited. Fix the source first: gutters, grading, a drain tile or a sump that actually runs. Flooring cannot fix a wet basement.

items.title: Check flatness and cracks
items.text: Basement slabs pitch toward drains and crack along control joints. Carpet hides almost all of that. Click-lock vinyl plank does not, so low spots get patched and high spots get ground before planks go down.

items.title: Plan the heat
items.text: A slab in February sits in the low 50s. Carpet with a good pad feels warm to bare feet. Vinyl plank feels like the slab under it unless you add an underlayment with some insulation value or run a wall heater in that room.

blocks.text: Room by room: which floor wins where

head: Room in the basement or ADU
Our usual pick
Why
rows: Mud, wet boots and dog paws come in here. Plank wipes clean; carpet at an exterior door in Snohomish is brown by March.
Spills, a dishwasher line and a fridge. One leak under carpet means tearing it out.
Standing water is a certainty at some point. Carpet does not belong here.
Warmth underfoot, quiet, and the softest landing for kids and older parents. Use a moisture-barrier pad below grade.
Sound absorption matters more in a concrete box than anywhere else in the house. Carpet and pad soak up the echo.
Rolling chairs and dropped dumbbells wear carpet fast. A dense low-pile carpet works; plank works better.
blocks.note: A transition strip at each doorway lets you change floors cleanly. Plan the doors so the transitions land under them, not in the middle of a hallway.

blocks.text: If you carpet below grade, this is the spec that survives

items.html: Synthetic fiber only. Nylon, triexta or a good polyester. They do not hold moisture the way wool does and they do not feed mold. Nylon takes the most abuse, which matters in a rental ADU.
A moisture-barrier pad. A rebond pad with a sealed film face keeps slab vapor and small spills from soaking into the cushion. This is the single most important line on a basement carpet order.
Low, dense pile. A tight loop or a short dense cut pile dries faster if something does go wrong and resists the crushing that heavy furniture on a slab causes.
Tack strip made for concrete. Regular tack strip pins pull out of old slab. Concrete-pin strip or an adhesive strip holds the stretch for the life of the carpet.
Seams away from the wet side. If the room has an exterior wall that has ever been damp, the seam goes on the other side. We lay this out with you during the measure.

blocks.text: If you choose vinyl plank, here is what matters underground

items.text: SPC (stone-plastic core) planks stay flat over a cold slab and shrug off temperature swings between a heated bedroom and an unheated storage room. Thin flexible planks telegraph every slab flaw.
Many planks have an attached pad, but below grade you still want a barrier. Either a plank whose attached pad is rated for concrete, or a separate vapor-rated underlayment. Never stack two pads.
items.note: Check the plank warranty: most void below-grade coverage if the slab moisture reading is above their limit.

items.d: Expansion gap at every wall and post
items.text: Basements have furnace platforms, posts and stair stringers. Each one needs the same gap as a wall. Pinning a floating floor at a post is how it buckles in July.
Basement stairs usually stay carpeted, which is fine. The plank at the bottom needs a proper stair nose or a transition so the last tread does not become a trip edge.

blocks.text: ADU realities: renters, noise and the county

a.title: Lean toward vinyl plank when
items: You will not see the floor between tenants
The unit has its own exterior entry straight into living space
You want one floor type and fewer transitions
You would rather replace a plank than a room of carpet

b.tag: Family use, aging parent, teen suite
b.title: Lean toward carpet when
items: Someone will sleep down there every night
The room above is a bedroom and you want quiet
The slab tested dry and the basement has never flooded
Warmth underfoot matters more than wipe-clean

blocks.title: One Snohomish-specific note:
blocks.text: Many rural properties here are on well water and septic. If the ADU adds a bathroom and laundry, the sewer ejector pit or septic pump usually lives in that floor. Keep hard flooring around the pit lid and make sure the lid stays accessible. We have pulled up a lot of carpet that was glued over one.
Mistakes we pull out of Snohomish basements

items.html: Carpet straight onto the slab with a standard pad. Two winters later the pad smells and the backing has a dark bloom. A barrier pad costs a little more per yard and prevents all of it.
Laminate in a basement. It looks like plank, but the core is wood fiber. One overflowing utility sink swells the seams for good. Choose vinyl plank below grade, not laminate.
Skipping the moisture test to save a day. The test is cheap and takes a weekend. The floor it protects is not cheap.
Carpet in a room with a floor drain. The drain is there because someone expected water. Respect that.
Finishing the floor before the framing and drywall are done. Drywall dust and dropped screws ruin new carpet and scratch new plank. Flooring goes in last, after paint.
Get a slab moisture reading in writing. Ask us to do it at the free estimate. The number decides your pad and your plank warranty.
Draw the zones on the plan. Mark each room carpet or plank and put every transition under a door. Read our basement carpet post for what a below-grade carpet order should say.
Ask for both samples at the same visit. Our mobile showroom brings carpet and vinyl plank boards together, so you can see the carpet color next to the plank color in your own basement light.
Schedule flooring after paint and trim. Baseboards can go on before carpet if you leave the right gap; for plank we prefer to set them after.
Keep the paperwork. Pad spec, plank moisture limit and our 1-year workmanship warranty all go in one folder with the ADU permit.

faq.q: Is carpet a bad idea in a Snohomish basement?
faq.a: Not if the slab tests reasonably dry, the basement has never flooded, and you use a synthetic carpet on a moisture-barrier pad. Carpet is a bad idea in basement rooms with a floor drain, an exterior door, plumbing appliances or a history of seepage. Zone those rooms in vinyl plank instead.

faq.q: Can I put vinyl plank and carpet in the same open basement room?
faq.a: Yes. A common layout runs plank from the exterior door across the kitchenette and stops at a straight line where the sitting area begins, with a flush transition strip. It looks intentional if the line follows a beam, a change in ceiling height or a furniture edge.

faq.q: Do I need a vapor barrier under carpet on concrete?
faq.a: Below grade, yes. Use a rebond pad with a sealed moisture-barrier film on top rather than a loose plastic sheet, which bunches and traps water. The pad does the job and stays put under the stretch.

faq.q: Will vinyl plank be freezing cold in a Snohomish basement?
faq.a: It will feel like the slab, which sits around 50 to 55 degrees in winter. A plank with a thicker attached pad or a separate insulating underlayment helps, and area rugs in the sitting area help more. Bedrooms are where carpet earns its place.

faq.q: Which floor is better for a rental ADU?
faq.a: Vinyl plank in most of the unit, because you cannot control pets, spills or how often it gets vacuumed. If you want one carpeted bedroom for comfort, choose a dense nylon on a barrier pad so it can be cleaned between tenants.

faq.q: Does the flooring go in before or after the ADU inspection?
faq.a: Rough inspections happen before flooring. Final inspection usually wants the finished floor in place, especially at the stairs and any egress. Schedule the flooring after drywall and paint, and keep the transition and stair-nose details ready for the inspector.
